title: Tool fires on the wrong messages? Check the description first
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Rewrite: when to use, when not, inputs
Description is detailed, model still slips on edge cases
Misroutes follow words in the system prompt
Call must never happen without a condition
One tool does two clearly different jobs
rule: Descriptions are the main selection signal. When one is a vague line, rewrite it with when-to-use and when-not-to-use before adding examples or hooks.

title: Two tools getting confused: which lever first?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Similar tools, one-line descriptions, mix-ups across many phrasings
Rewrite descriptions: purpose, inputs, when to use the other tool
Descriptions already clear, mix-ups follow certain words
Rewrite the wording that ties those words to a tool
Descriptions clear, a few hard cases still wrong
One tool does several jobs through a catch-all input
Tools must be called in a fixed order
rule: Descriptions are the main way Claude picks a tool. When two tools overlap, give each a clear purpose and a when-to-use-the-other line before adding examples or machinery.

title: A tool keeps being called wrongly: which layer fixes it?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Good description, catch-all parameter still misused
Split into purpose-specific tools with typed inputs
Bad input reaches the tool and fails vaguely
Valid empty result confused with a failure
rule: When good descriptions do not stop misuse of a catch-all input, split the tool into purpose-specific tools with defined inputs.

title: Wrong tool picked? Diagnose by the pattern of the mistakes
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Wrong tool picked randomly, descriptions are one-liners
Expand descriptions: inputs, examples, when not to use
Descriptions already good, but misroutes always follow certain words
Something else that mentions those words: the system prompt or examples
Find and rewrite that wording in terms of the customer's goal
One tool does two different jobs
Wrong order of calls that must never happen
Agent answers in text when it must call a tool
rule: Descriptions are the main signal, not the only one. If misroutes follow specific words and the descriptions are already good, look for those words in the system prompt.

title: Agent misroutes calls: description problem or tool-design problem?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Misroutes, descriptions already detailed, one tool hides different contracts
Failed call looks like an empty result
Too many tools on one agent
rule: Descriptions first. But when one tool hides several jobs with different inputs and outputs, split it into purpose-specific tools.

title: Claude picks the wrong tool: what can you change?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Wrong pick, descriptions are minimal, you own the server
Rewrite descriptions: inputs, outputs, example, when to use a sibling
Descriptions good, but one tool does several jobs
Split or rename into purpose-specific tools
Results need cleaning before the model sees them
rule: If you own the tool and Claude picks wrong, fix the description first.

title: Tool called badly? Ask what the model was told about it
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Add input format, examples, edge cases
Bad calls happen and the agent can't recover
One generic tool does several jobs
rule: Minimal description → bad calls. First step: input format, examples, edge cases and boundaries in the description.
